Tone may have both a lexical and a grammatical function. || Boyeldieu 1988: 282: «Tun, lua et 'ba connaissent des systèmes tonals à 3 registres (avec différentes modulations possibles) dont l'unité fonctionnelle serait plutôt représentée par le schème tonal du "mot" dans son ensemble.»
new_statements.translation: 1988 passage: 'Tun, Lua and Ɓa have tone systems with 3 registers (with various possible modulations), whose functional unit would rather be the tonal pattern of the "word" as a whole.'

new_statements.locator: §4.4 'Tones', p.71 (PDF p.20); corroborating earlier statement: Boyeldieu 1988 §2.1 p.282 (file)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (75 pp., publisher-paginated, open download from florianlionnet.com): extracted text of PDF p.20 = printed p.71 shows section '4.4 Tones' opening exactly as quoted: 'Ɓa, Lua, Tun, and Bolgo have tone systems with three contrastive heights (Low, Mid, and High), with frequent contour tones (e.g. L͡H H͡M, M͡L, etc.), not restricted to long vowels. Tone may have both a lexical and a grammatical function.' Footnote 24 on the same page confirms the Ɓa data are Boyeldieu's 1984 Korbol speaker plus Lionnet/Hoïnathy 2011-2016. The section continues (p.72) with Lua verb-class tone and the Kulaal two-tone caveat; nothing on stress. a full-text search for stress/accent over the full text for stres…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ɓa is described only as a three-height (L/M/H) lexical and grammatical tone language whose tone patterns are organised over the word; no published source says anything about word stress or accent placement. (Lionnet 2017 slides additionally list Ba among Middle-Chari languages with stem-initial segmental prominence, C1/V1 richer than later positions, but give no stress rule.)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement refers to the lexical word ('schème tonal du mot'); Ɓa data are Boyeldieu's own 1984 field notes plus Lionnet's 2011-16 notes (Magalya dialect, Korbol), reported inside comparative overviews rather than a dedicated description.
new_statements.identity_note: Statements concern Ɓa proper (buaa1245, ISO bub; 'ba in Boyeldieu 1988). Boyeldieu's data come from one Ɓa speaker recorded in 1984 (dialect unstated); Lionnet's from the Magalya dialect spoken in and around Korbol. Korom/Kawãwãy (Tilé Nougar; c. 60-300 speakers) is treated by Lionnet as at least a very divergent dialect of Ɓa, possibly a separate language (no separate glottocode known to me); it is not covered by the quoted statements. Boyeldieu & Palayer 1975, listed by Glottolog under bub, actually describes Lua/Niellim (niel1243) and Tunia (tuni1251), not Ɓa.
